memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, 'There is the sound of war in the camp.' Moses replied: 'It is not the sound of victory, it is not the sound of defeat; it is the sound of singing that I hear.'" - Exod 32:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A small, almost cinematic moment. Joshua, the soldier, hears the noise and assumes battle. Moses, who has just come from God's presence, hears it differently. It is not war. It is a party.

There is wisdom here. Joshua's ears were trained for one kind of danger. Moses had been with God, and he perceived the situation truly.

Time in God's presence changes what we notice. We start to see what is actually happening rather than what we expect to see. We begin to recognise that some of the loudest celebrations in this world are, in fact, the sound of people running from God — and that is far more dangerous than an army.

It is worth asking what our own celebrations sound like from heaven's side. Not all joy is holy joy. Israel was singing, and God was grieved.

Jesus wept over Jerusalem while the city carried on as normal (Luke 19:41-42). To walk closely with Him is to gain His perspective — to feel joy where He rejoices and sorrow where He grieves. That kind of discernment is not natural. It comes from spending time with Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you assume about situations before you bring them to God?
2. Has time with God changed how you see the world around you?
3. Is there a celebration in your life that God might see differently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me Your eyes and Your ears. Let time in Your presence reshape how I see everything else. Amen.
